# nora

27. Age-group triathlete, Aarhus, Denmark, AGF-Tri club. Three years of
record: a year building, a peak with several personal bests, then eighteen
months where the numbers quietly stop adding up. Synthetic; any resemblance
to a real person is accidental and unintended.

## In her own words

"I used to be able to tell you my splits from memory. Now I look at a
session and the pace is slower than it was two years ago at the same heart
rate, every time, and I still write down the same plate of food I planned to
eat that morning whether I ate it or not. I know what that looks like on
paper. I am not going to pretend I don't.

The camp we didn't go to this year - I told the squad it was money. It
wasn't only that. I'm not writing down what the rest of it was, here or
anywhere else. Some things I keep for myself. The magpies, the score with
a friend on our local segments, whether a session felt easy - none of that
is in any app, and it's not going in one now either.

The foot thing has a name, the clinic gave me that, and I don't mind saying
it. There's a different thing going on that doesn't have a name I'm willing
to say out loud, not to a coach, not to a screen, not really to myself. If
you're looking for it in here, you'll find one line about missing something
three months running, and that's all you get."

## The record her life produces

- Three years: 2027-07-01 to 2030-06-30. Ascend year, peak, then an
  eighteen-month decline.
- Sessions: 1,469 rows across swim, cycle and run, watch-connector
  throughout. The first 494 rows (the whole ascend year) carry only the
  founding key set; every row from 2028-07-01 carries the full current
  shape - the same watch, a richer sync from that point on.
- Weight: daily, from a connected scale. 56.2 kg at the record's start,
  peaking around 58.6 kg near October 2028, ending at 50.6 kg.
- Daily: two rows most days, a watch row (steps, energy out, resting heart
  rate, sleep) and an app row (energy in). The app row never really moves:
  2,050-2,200 kcal, every day, for three years.
- Medical: one episode, a right foot stress reaction diagnosed at a running
  clinic in February 2030, athlete-stated, status moving from active to
  monitoring as the return-to-run checks clear.
- Goals: an externally verified qualifying slot (achieved), two attested
  performance targets the schema has no field for, and a coach-set guarded
  volume cap.
- Achievements: an olympic-distance PB, an FTP bump, an open-water PB, and
  the qualifying slot itself, all in the first two years.

## The axis she stresses

An intake figure that never moves while the training load, the resting
heart rate, and the scale all move against it. A prescribed volume cut she
appears to comply with in the record and does not comply with in life. A
diagnosis she is perfectly willing to name, sitting three months away in
the same file from a line about something she will never name at all. And
a training partner who is there in the data and then, one date, permanently
is not, without a single row ever saying why.
